dedupe_keys.name: stics soil crop model and javastics

description: STICS is a dynamic, generic soil-atmosphere-crop model developed since the late 1990s by several research institutes, for researchers, teachers and agricultural professionals. It is deterministic, mechanistic and runs on a daily step. It simulates energy, water, carbon and nitrogen balances through the crop cycle. It covers annual crops, two-species intercrops, perennials such as grassland, vines and Miscanthus, cover crops, and bare soil. A simulation covers one homogeneous unit of soil, climate and practices, for one cycle or a multi-year sequence. Inputs are soil horizon properties, daily climate and farming practices: tillage, sowing, organic and mineral fertiliser, irrigation and foliage management. Coverage is generic. Access is free after registering on the download site: STICS and JavaSTICS 10.5.0 (page modified 14 September 2026). STICS is under CeCILL-C, the JavaSTICS interface under CeCILL-B, and the R packages under LGPL on GitHub. A free book (Beaudouin et al., 2023) documents the model. Caveats: the team disclaims warranties, other contexts of use need a specific agreement, and the programming language was not stated on the pages read. For simulation it gives crop yield, water and nitrogen responses to drought, heat and practices for adaptation and agro-ecological transition studies. Related catalogue records include DSSAT, APSIM and PCSE/WOFOST.
